newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures slump at end, seen floundering.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures slump at end, seen floundering.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures dived through a long-standing support late on Friday, ending on a weak note and sparking predictions of more gloom in the days ahead.

Dealers said growing concerns about Japan's economy against a backdrop of brokerage scandals, construction sector woes and depressed car sales, kicked in to push the 225-share Nikkei average below the 20,000 level.
Its September futures ended 550 points lower at 19,795, their weakest close in just under three weaks. Market turnover was an active 19,700 lots.
A senior dealer at a European institution said the selling was exacerbated by rumours U.S. financier George Soros was selling the Nikkei and buying Japanese government bonds.
Dealers said the September Nikkei's slide was intensified by stop-loss sales below 20,000 points and the contract would now have trouble recovering to that level.
"This is the fourth time it tried to break 20,000. It may still try to go down to 19,500," a trader at another European futures house said.
"Let's see tonight's non-farm payrolls. But I think sentiment for the Nikkei will be really bad unless we see some sign that the (Japanese) economy is improving," the first dealer said.
The release of U.S. non-farm payrolls data at 1230 GMT could provide some respite to the Nikkei if the numbers are non-inflationary and spark a rally on Wall Street, dealers said.
